findings.title: concepts.md's Archive section still says a failed brief save never stops the archive, and never mentions the sign-off
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the end of the Archive section (docs/concepts.md:276-278) so it matches orbit-archive-modifications as modified: with `signoff: change` the archive shows the saved brief and asks you to sign off or decline before anything is merged, and a brief that cannot be saved stops the archive (there is nothing to sign); under every other value a failed save is noted in the archive's record and never stops it. Add the same step to the `/orbit:archive` 'Before the move, it:' list in docs/commands.md:218-224 (and the bulk-archive paragraph), naming the `signoff` key. Task 5.1 named only the Trail row of concepts.md, so these two pages were outside the sweep.
findings.reproduction: docs/concepts.md:277-278 reads 'a brief that cannot be saved is noted in the archive's record and never stops the archive.' The archive body's save table (src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts, BRIEF_SAVE_STEP failure row) now says 'under `change` the hold stops it, since there is no copy to sign', and SIGNOFF_HOLD_STEP's third row stops the archive before the sync on a failed save. docs/commands.md:218-224 lists what the archive does before the move and names neither the save nor the sign-off.

findings.title: Two docs sentences overstate what the reader checks under `signoff: change`
findings.recommendation: docs/customization.md:62 says the reading step reads the account 'so the brief you sign has been checked by a reader' — only the account (and the decision records) are read, and an account a walk replaces after the system review reaches no reader before archive (design.md's Risks names this). Say 'so the account in the brief you sign has been checked by a reader, unless a later fix replaced it'. docs/cli.md:430 says the brief lists 'the records no reader has checked, the account included' — under `change` a read account is listed nowhere; say 'the account included when no reader has checked it'.

findings.title: account.ts's header still says the selection never takes the account
findings.recommendation: The module comment (src/core/account.ts:13-14) says the account is kept outside decisions/ 'so no reader of the decision-record selection (`selectUnreadRecords`) takes it'. Since this change, selectUnreadRecords takes the latest account under `signoff: change`. Reword to: 'outside decisions/, so the decision-record chains never include it; the selection takes the latest account only under signoff: change (`The reader takes the account only when sign-off is per change`).'

findings.title: `orbit brief --hold` with no --change says "'undefined' is not a single change name"
findings.recommendation: In BriefCommand.hold, refuse a missing --change before the single-name check, for example: "--hold takes --change <name>: `orbit brief --change <name> --hold`." (the --save path already has the same message). The test at test/core/signoff.test.ts:327 says 'or with nothing' in its title but never runs `brief --hold` alone; add that case so the title matches what it checks.
findings.reproduction: `node bin/orbit.js brief --hold` prints "orbit brief: 'undefined' is not a single change name." and exits 1.

findings.title: The hold's check on a stored sign-off is narrower than 'a shape the write gate would refuse'
findings.recommendation: orbit-program-brief's hold requirement fails the hold on a latest sign-off 'that has a shape the write gate would refuse'. checkStoredSignoff (src/core/signoff.ts:138-144) checks `command`, `sha256` and the payload fields, but not the spine the gate also enforces (`timestamp` and `model` present, `change` a string) or unknown keys. A hand-edited latest record missing `model` would still lift the hold. Either add those checks to checkStoredSignoff, or narrow the spec sentence to the fields the hold relies on.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Add the spine checks (timestamp, model present, change a string equal to the change) and an unknown-key check to checkStoredSignoff, with a test showing each refusal.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Narrow the spec's sentence to 'has a command, sha256, brief or answer the write gate would refuse', matching the code.

findings.title: The silent-reading refusal calls an owed account a 'decision record'
findings.recommendation: Under `signoff: change` the owed list can hold an account, and the refusal reads 'this pass owes a reading of 1 decision record(s) (account-…)'. Say 'record(s)' (or 'decision record(s) or account') here, as the read-list shape refusal a few lines above already does ('or account-<TS>.json under signoff: change').

commentary:
Probed the engine side hardest: resolveSignoffSetting (read only by its three callers; readProjectConfig does not parse the key, so orbit status prints nothing new), computeHold (the setting read first, no folder read when off, latest-only reads that fail rather than fall back), the signoff write gate (scope, setting, latest copy, engine sha256, child identity, collision bump), and every selectUnreadRecords caller (brief, owed list and read-list check, archive count, orbit brief).
I ran the CLI against this repo: `--hold` with no key reports off, a doc and an archived name are refused with nothing on stdout, and `orbit brief --change program-brief` renders byte-identical output twice, so the 'same text is not asked again' row holds in practice. The full suite passes (198 files, 4185 tests) and `validate program-brief --strict` is clean.
Pass 0 and the drift sweep ran inline: invoking verify-change or audit-drift would have written their own run summaries into this change's trail from a dispatched worker. No lenses exist, so the perspective and critical-path passes had nothing to walk.
The one real gap is in the docs: the narrative pages were written for brief-render and still describe the save as harmless. The other findings are edges and wording. The reading-finding walk (an account replaced in a walk) is instructed in the body but the walk gate is not exercised with an account path by any test. It mirrors the decision-record path, which works, so I note it here and do not raise it as a finding.

direction.reasoning:
The sign-off is built as designed. At the defaults it is inert: no folder is read and nothing is asked. Under `change` the hold fails closed: a damaged latest record never revives an earlier signature, and a signature lifts the hold only over identical bytes.
Walk the concepts.md Archive section before archive. It now contradicts the archive's behaviour under `change`, and a user turning the key on would read it first. The rest are small fixes that can ride the same walk.
